method: Direct complete original image inspection via view_image detail=original. Coordinator review, not blinded to the arm progress report. No inferred off-frame endpoint.

observations.evidence: A uniformed auditor overlooks two adults exchanging a broken token beside a sealed paper, wrist cuff, ledger and two glowing cut filament ends in a ruined ceremonial room.
The left adult retains the reference-like dark short bob, separated fringe and facial impression; identity is not established.
Two matching broken silver token halves are shown across the adjacent open palms; both adult owners remain distinct.
The younger adult grips a stamp whose base touches an amber wax seal on the paper.
The visible cuff encircles the same forearm whose open hand supports the token. The authored setup requires the cuff on the other arm.
The ledger is clear and a small eyelet sits near it, but the filament-to-ledger attachment cannot be traced as a legible continuous bound endpoint.
Two separated hot tips and faint rising smoke are visible on the table.
The two hot cut ends lie on the bare table well to the right of the stamp/wax seal; the split is not located at the authored intervening seal.

whole_case_basis: The pre-render complete oath-release mechanism requires all named arm, ledger, seal and cut-end components together. Wrong arm ownership and unclear ledger attachment fail it.
limits: No new source was used; genre and institutional appearance do not establish data contribution.
Political history, former household roles, actual coercion, legal release and moral inversion remain narrative interpretations.
